first.rationale: Verify the two decision-critical claims: whether promotional pricing produced durable qualified revenue rather than short-term discounted acquisition, and whether shorter onboarding improved downstream revenue quality beyond early adoption. Current intent favors simplifying onboarding because completion and activation are both declining, while pricing carries greater margin and cohort-quality risk. Final commitment remains contingent on the archived records.

final.rationale: Run a standard experiment shortening onboarding. The verified source shows higher completion, faster time-to-value, and a modest 30-day retention gain, directly addressing both current onboarding and activation declines while supporting sustainable qualified revenue. Reject promotional pricing for this slot because its verified retention decline undermines long-term cohort value despite short-term acquisition gains. Retain uncertainty about performance under current conditions by testing rather than broadly rolling out.
